retainedReference.title: Serapeum of Alexandria
retainedReference.reason: No unique physical footprint or centerline with exact Wikidata identity has been resolved.

pictures.author: Iris Fernandez / AWIB-ISAW
pictures.observations: Full portrait photo inspected: shaft and leafy capital silhouette, two separate frontal sphinxes and plinths, rough excavated terrace edge. No pixels copied.

pictures.author: Iris Fernandez / AWIB-ISAW
pictures.observations: Full wide photo inspected: same column and paired sphinxes in an open low limestone excavation; uneven walls/steps and modern visitor rope path remain context. No intact large temple mass visible.

pictures.author: Iris Fernandez / AWIB-ISAW
pictures.observations: Complete ordinary closer front image actually inspected: worn frontal head, broken central forehead ornament, broad nemes flaps, long tapering chest, paired front paws on a rough original block over a pale trapezoidal restored plinth with a torus/lipped top. Back/body depth remains an approximate crouching mass; no exact carving or inscriptions claimed.

componentIdentity.basis: The candidate is the Serapeum site Q521646. Its reference coordinate is about 88m southeast of the actual named column point. Standard PMTiles monument17593449217372 fixes the component center at29.8963925242424,31.182580653236712; the ordinary OpenStreetMap node1263172956 page confirms Pompei's Pillar and component Q492487. These are deliberately distinct site/component identities. The ordinary site photographs explicitly show this column and paired sphinxes as the Serapeum remains. mappedIdentity records that reviewed constituent association, not an assertion that the node has the site's QID. Native +X east/+Z south, runtime heading0. Approximate southeast-facing sphinx arrangement follows the photographed viewpoint; their spacing and bearing are picture-led estimates, not surveyed plans.
